Fitting and completing heights

Source: vignettes/fill-missing-heights.Rmd
fill-missing-heights.Rmd

fit_height() fits height from diameter by species. A group vector adds supported group effects. complete_heights() retains finite heights and fills missing or nonfinite values.

Fit measured heights 

## Select retained height measurements
measured <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  filter(!is.na(ht_observed))
## Fit height by species with plot effects
fit <- fit_height(dbh = measured$dbh,
                  ht = measured$ht_observed,
                  spcd = measured$spcd,
                  group = measured$plot)
spcd model_key pooled a b c
202 spcd_202 FALSE 211.055 0.053 1.355
263 spcd_263 FALSE 412.085 0.009 0.758

pooled identifies species using the pooled relationship. Species with too few measurements or unsuccessful separate fits use that relationship. Available forms are chapman_richards, curtis, wykoff, naslund, and schumacher.

## Draw measured heights and fitted curves
plot(fit)

Complete inventory heights 

## Retain observed heights and fill the missing values
trees <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  mutate(ht = complete_heights(dbh = dbh,
                               ht = ht_observed,
                               spcd = spcd,
                               group = plot,
                               fit = fit))
tree species dbh ht_observed ht
2 Douglas-fir 10.42 NA 70.229
3 Douglas-fir 12.21 NA 81.273
5 western hemlock 36.09 NA 173.681
6 western hemlock 9.82 NA 67.614
8 Douglas-fir 14.31 NA 93.132

Pass a fitted object to reuse the same model across data groups. With fit = NULL, completion fits from the supplied observations.

Predict heights

predict_height() predicts every supplied tree. re_form = 'population' omits fitted group effects. Groups absent from the fit use its population relationship. Species absent from the fit receive missing predictions.

## Predict heights for the complete shipped tree list
predictions <- predict_height(fit = fit,
                              dbh = example_trees$dbh,
                              spcd = example_trees$spcd,
                              re_form = 'population',
                              interval = TRUE,
                              seed = 7)
fit lower upper
79.959 70.824 89.808
85.928 75.740 96.077
102.809 93.947 111.895
101.713 90.758 112.705
122.425 113.243 131.393
123.031 110.497 136.000

With interval = TRUE, the result contains fit, lower, and upper. Simulated limits include group variation and residual error with coefficients held fixed. They exclude coefficient uncertainty and inventory sampling uncertainty.
